editorial:
Imagine spending twenty years in a cell only to realize the outside world is actually scarier than prison. You meet a former barber who did something terrible out of jealousy a long time ago. Now that he is finally free, he expects a warm welcome and a fresh start. Instead, he finds a world that has moved on without him. The vibe is a strange mix of funny and sad, showing you how hard it is to fit back into a society that feels fake and cold. You will feel for him as he tries to figure out where he actually belongs.

What really works here is the acting and the way it shows the fake behavior of his family. While the pacing is a bit slower than modern films, the emotional payoff is worth it. It is a great pick if you like stories about people fighting to find their place. If you want the best experience, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for those crisp old-school visuals. You could also rent it on Apple TV if you are in a hurry, but adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go for movie buffs.
endingExplained: After trying to live with his family and friends, the main character realizes that the freedom he wanted is actually a lie. He sees that the people around him are selfish and hypocritical. He cannot handle the pressure and the fake kindness of the world. In the end, he decides that he is happier and safer in prison. He chooses to go back behind bars because it is the only place where he feels at peace.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves character studies and old Italian cinema.
